paragraphs: Persuasive advertising, despite its irrefutable economic benefits, can entail social drawbacks. There are strong cases to be made for both sides of the argument.

On the one hand, supporters of advertising often point to the undeniable economic benefits it can bring. As a result, production is encouraged, creating more employment opportunities and greater state revenue through taxation. This naturally results in a stronger economy. To illustrate, e-commerce platforms such as Shopee and Lazada in Vietnam rely heavily on advertising campaigns to attract customers, boosting both their sales and the entire digital retail sector. In addition, the advertising industry creates direct jobs in marketing, media and design.

Those on the other side of the debate, however, argue that advertising entails negative social consequences. Advertisements constantly show images of perfect lifestyles, beauty standards and luxury possessions, which may foster dissatisfaction among viewers. For example, young people may feel pressured to buy trendy clothes or the latest smart gadgets advertised on TikTok and Facebook, leading to frustration when they cannot afford them. Furthermore, repeated exposure to these messages may promote materialistic values and a money-driven culture in the long run.
In conclusion, both views are valid to a certain extent. Advertising plays a crucial role in economic development, while its idealised messages may also contribute to social dissatisfaction.

paragraphs: I believe that news media have too much influence on people's lives today. Although some people regard this influence as a negative development, I believe that it brings both drawbacks and benefits.

The news media have a considerable influence on daily life. With regard to the reasons for this influence, one contributing factor is the widespread access to smartphones and the Internet, as these technologies allow people to follow the news instantly. Therefore, wherever and whenever they are, news becomes a regular part of their routine every day. Another significant driver of this influence is the intense competition among news outlets. In order to gain attention, most media agencies focus on shocking and breaking content. Additionally, they present it in a highly sensationalized manner with dramatic headlines and eye-catching visuals. In this sense, this approach reinforces the overall impact of news on public opinion.

This situation has given rise to both negative and beneficial effects. Admittedly, exposure to a constant stream of distressing and exaggerated news can overwhelm people. They feel overly anxious and helpless, even in situations that do not directly affect them. However, news coverage warns the public to existing and looming problems in society. For instance, reports on crime, natural disasters, or political corruption will make individuals better informed and more prepared to respond to potential threats. In this way, individuals can handle risks in an increasingly complex society.

In conclusion, I believe that the news media's considerable influence on people's lives today stems from varied causes and can bring both adverse effects and benefits. Although distressing news can create anxiety, its role in keeping people informed should not be overlooked.

paragraphs: Some people believe that schools should reward students with the best academic results, while others believe that recognizing students who have made progress deserves greater attention. From my perspective, there are strong cases to be made for rewarding both groups.

Supporters of rewarding top achievers argue that schools should reward students with the best academic results. The first reason is that these students have diligently applied themselves to their studies. They therefore deserve their praise and privileges. This may encourage these students and others to study harder to win rewards. As a result, their effort may raise academic performance overall. Furthermore, this kind of competition is seen in almost every aspect of life, where only the best individuals are rewarded. This means that students can become used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, which may enable them to achieve success in later life.

Advocates of rewarding progress argue that schools should also reward students who show improvements. To begin with, if only a few high-achieving students receive rewards, this can cause others to think that their effort is futile. This is because they cannot surpass those outstanding individuals. These students are prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened and may gradually lose the incentive to study. Furthermore, rewarding progress can encourage all students to be diligent in their studies and help students to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves. They can continue to improve irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. The desire to outdo themselves may benefit them more than the determination to defeat others.
Overall, it seems to me that both views are valid to a certain extent. Schools should reward both students with the best academic results and those who have made progress.

paragraphs: In some countries, parents opt to educate their children at home rather than send them to school. Although such development is beneficial to a certain extent, I believe that the disadvantages that it offers are far more pronounced.

Admittedly, supporters of homeschooling argue that this trend can bring some merits. First, it may allow parents to save money as they do not have to pay school fees. Second, children educated at home are less likely to experience bullying and peer pressure, both of which can cause emotional and mental problems. Added to this is that parents teaching their children at home by themselves tailor their curriculum and pedagogical approaches to best suit their young ones. This is often not the case in traditional schooling due to the large class size.

However, I believe that the substantial detriments of this development far outweigh the positives. Initially, this educational approach may not actually save money as parents may need to pay a large amount of money for lab equipment and tutors. One parent may also need to reduce working hours. This is primarily because they need to cater for their child's needs, be these academic or personal. Moreover, most parents are not well versed in all school subjects, which can cause difficulties in properly explaining concepts to children and ultimately lead to academic problems. Finally, children can face social problems at school, such as bullying and having romantic feelings for others. These experiences can prepare them for social and workplace situations in the future.

In conclusion, although it is true that homeschooling may bring about a few advantages, these are relatively minor and should not overshadow the far more significant and long-lasting drawbacks it entails.
